Could students solve the irreproducibility crisis?

Terribly unfair to students. If PhDs want studies checked they should check them. Maybe make reproduction a part of the publishing processs. As in we look at reproduced studies in a different way than one hit wonders.
I like the suggestion about making it part of the whole publishing process. Not sure how it would all work out, but it sounds like it would help solve the issue.

The way I see it working is that we make people note it on their CV. So if we have a guy with 20 published studies but none have been reproduced we would weigh that a lot lower than a guy with 5 solidly reproduced studies. This would encourage people to talk their colleagues into reproducing the studies. And there would be some quid pro quo going on. If there is truly a backlog and its an issue, the journals could also push it by requiring a reproduction before publishing any new study. That equally burdens all the scientists as apposed to just putting it on grad students.

Sodium Bicarbonate is messy and dangerous because of the foaming mess. I've heard that uria is best, but I've also heard that one shouldn't add organic chemicals to nitric. What is best and also easily accessible to home experimenters?
What is the best way to neutralize concentrated Nitric Acid?

Sodium carbonate is a good way to go. Carbon Dioxide is evolved as a by product which helps reduce the exotherm. Do not add organics to nitric acid. This will only foam if you're adding it too quickly. It should also be done inside a fume cupboard really, wearing appropriate gloves, lab coat and eyewaer (visor if possible).

1)Calculate the required concentration and quantity required to neutralize all of the nitric acid (use a dilute solution to dissipate the heat.). Add 20% more to be safe.

2)Add crushed Ice to the dilute carbonate.

3)While gently swirling the carbonate solution, add the nitric to it drop wise from a separating funnel. (funnel in clamp stand)

4)Add more crushed ice as required.

5)Repeat until finished

You can neutralize it with sodium hydroxide fairly easily. If you use a somewhat dilute NaOH solution (compared to your HNO3) and add it slowly you shouldn't get too much heating. It is often found in the form of 100% lye drain cleaner.
